title: The Premium Grace Period and Termination for Non-Payment on a Ridgecrest Advantage Plan
content:
A monthly premium charge still unpaid after its due day puts a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan enrollment into the premium grace period, and the member is sent a delinquency notice naming the amount owed and the last day of that grace period.

### How the grace period is counted

The grace period runs for the number of calendar days the plan held fixes, counted from the day the plan posted the first unpaid monthly premium charge. Calendar days are counted from the day after that posting date, every day of the week counts including weekends and public holidays, the last day of the grace period is itself still inside the grace period, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days.

**Condition of record for termination.** The plan has not received the full outstanding premium by the last day of the grace period counted from the day the plan posted the first unpaid monthly premium charge. The premium account and the enrollment record are the authority, tested before the termination is processed and read together on the enrollment reference and the reference of that charge.

### Cure, partial payment and termination

Where the full outstanding premium reaches the plan at any time before that day ends, the enrollment returns to coverage in force with no break in coverage and keeps its original coverage effective date. A partial payment does not cure the delinquency however small the remainder, and it never restarts the clock: the grace period keeps running on the original posting date. Termination for non-payment ends coverage on the last day of the month in which the grace period expired, and the disenrollment reason recorded is non-payment of premium.

### Coverage during the grace period

While the enrollment is in the grace period the member keeps full coverage and claims are adjudicated normally; the plan never withholds care during the grace period.

### Boundary cases

| Circumstance | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| The full outstanding premium reaches the plan on the day before the last day of the grace period | The delinquency is cured; coverage continues unbroken on its original effective date |
| The full outstanding premium reaches the plan on the last day of the grace period itself | The delinquency is cured; that day is still inside the grace period |
| The full outstanding premium reaches the plan on the day after the last day of the grace period | The grace period has expired with premium outstanding; coverage ends on the last day of the month in which it expired |
| Part of the outstanding premium reaches the plan on the last day of the grace period | Not cured; the grace period is still reckoned from the original posting date and has now expired |
